faq: Do my app's features have to change?
No. A redesign changes how screens look and flow, not what the app does. Your logic, data and settings stay as they are, so merchants find everything where they expect it.
Will the design follow Shopify's guidelines?
Yes. We build with Polaris, Shopify's own component library, so your app feels like part of the admin and stays easy to keep updated as Polaris evolves.
Will merchants need to do anything after the update?
No. The new screens appear when they next open the app. We write a short in-app note or changelog text if you want to tell them about the change.
Do you design in Figma before building?
Yes, for the first screens. You approve those mockups, then we build the rest in the same style. A full Figma file of every page is included in the Premium package.
desc:
Shopify app redesign with Polaris gives your admin screens a clear, native look inside Shopify. Ecom Swift LLC reviews how merchants move through your app, then redesigns and rebuilds the key pages while your features and data stay exactly as they are.

## Why does app design matter inside the Shopify admin?

Your app lives next to Shopify's own screens, so merchants compare it with them all day. If your pages look different, behave differently or confuse people, the app feels unreliable even when the code is sound. Polaris is Shopify's design system, and using it correctly makes your app familiar from the first click: the same spacing, buttons, tables, banners and form behavior merchants already know.

## What a redesign changes for merchants

Design problems show up as support tickets and uninstalls. A table with no empty state looks broken. A form with no inline errors leaves people guessing. A settings page that hides the main action makes merchants think the app does nothing.

A redesign fixes these by changing structure, not decoration. The most important action becomes obvious. Related settings are grouped. Errors say what went wrong and what to do. New merchants see a home page that tells them the next step instead of a blank dashboard.

## Why layout affects how merchants use your app

People scan, they do not read. A clear page hierarchy lets a merchant find what they need in a few seconds. Consistent patterns mean they learn the app once and then work faster. A setup guide helps new merchants reach their first result, which is where many installs are won or lost.

Mobile matters because many merchants manage their stores from the Shopify mobile app. Pages that need a wide screen are hard to use there, so we check both.

## What a strong app interface includes

- Polaris components used consistently across all screens.
- A home page that shows status and the next step.
- Clear page titles and one primary action on each page.
- Tables with search, filters and useful empty states.
- Forms with inline validation and helpful error messages.
- A setup guide or wizard for new merchants.
- Help links and short tips where merchants usually get stuck.
- Layouts that work on desktop and the Shopify mobile app.
- An accessibility pass: contrast, keyboard use and clear labels.

## How we work

We start by walking through your app as a new merchant and as a daily user, noting every point of friction. We agree the list of pages to redesign, then produce the new layouts and rebuild them in code. Your features, data and API logic remain untouched; this is a change to the interface layer.

The Basic package tidies a few key pages and adds clearer empty and error states, with before and after screenshots. Standard redesigns the home page and main screens and adds a setup guide, with a check in the Shopify mobile admin. Premium refreshes the whole interface, adds a step-by-step setup wizard and built-in help, includes an accessibility pass and provides an editable design file. Merchants do not need to do anything after the update.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Name the pages merchants use most, so those come first.
- Share support questions that point to confusing screens.
- Keep wording short and in the merchant's language.
- Use Polaris components before inventing custom ones.

**Avoid:**
- Adding new features during a visual refresh.
- Custom colors and fonts that clash with the admin.
- Long forms on a single page with no grouping.
- Redesigning every page at once with no priority.

## Who this service is for

App owners whose interface was built quickly and has never been reviewed. Developers who are strong at backend work but not at layout. Teams that plan a relaunch and want the app to feel ready for a wider audience.

## What we need from you

Repository access, collaborator access in your Partner Dashboard and a development store with the app installed. Share any brand notes and a list of known problem pages. We never ask for passwords, and we work from a branch so you can review everything before it goes live.
